entities.summary: William de Braose was the second Baron Braose, as well as Lord of Gower and Lord of Bramber. He was held as a hostage after being captured in 1264 during the Second Barons' War and records of some of his childhood expenses survive from his time as a hostage. He first entered royal service in 1286 and, in 1291, he succeeded his father as baron. He continued in royal military service, serving in Scotland as well as in Wales. Protracted disputes over his lands embroiled him throughout his life and at the end of his life helped spark a revolt against King Edward II of England's favourites, the Despensers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Lord of Gower and Lord of Bramber, William de Braose played a significant role in Welsh politics during the late 13th century. His disputes over his lands contributed to the Despenser Revolt against King Edward II's favourites.
